70:1: Abu Jaafar said: The reciters differed in their recitation of the phrase A questioner asked. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as A questioner asked with a hamza on the word A questioner asked, meaning a questioner from among the infidels asked about the punishment of God, about whom it would befall. Some of the reciters of Medina read it as A questioner asked, without adding a hamza on the word asked, and they explained this by saying that it is a verb from the root word to flood. The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads it with a hamza, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on that, and the fact that most of the people of interpretation from the Salaf interpreted it to mean a hamza. He mentioned the interpretation of this as well, and said its interpretation is similar to what we said about it: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, A questioner asked about a punishment that will come to pass, he said: That is the question of the infidels about the punishment of God, which is coming to pass. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: If this is the truth from You (al-Anfal 8:32)...the verse. He said: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass. Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asam told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, A questioner asked, he said: A supplicant called for a punishment to befall, he said: It will befall in the Hereafter. He said: It is their statement, O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky (al-Anfal 8:32). Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall him, he said: He asked about the punishment of God upon whom will it befall the disbelievers. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, A questioner asked, he said: He asked about a punishment that would befall, so God said, For the disbelievers there is none that can avert it. As for those who read it without a hamza, they said: The questioner is a valley from the valleys of Hell. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding the statement of God, A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass, he said: Some of the people of knowledge said: It is a valley in Hell called Sa’il. And his saying, with a punishment that will befall the disbelievers, means: He asked about a punishment that will befall the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of the verse for the disbelievers is for the disbelievers, like the one who: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, A punishment to befall * the disbelievers, that he said: It will befall the disbelievers, and the lam in His statement, to the disbelievers is from the connection of the word to befall. And His statement: There is no one who can avert it * from God, Lord of the Ascending Stairways. God Almighty says: There is no one who can avert the punishment that will befall the disbelievers from God.
70:2: God Almighty says: For the disbelievers there is no repeller.
70:3: And His saying, Possessor of the ascents, means: Possessor of the heights, degrees, virtues, and blessings. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, of the ascents, he said: the heights and virtues. Bishr told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: From God, the Possessor of Ascents means the Possessor of bounties and blessings. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, From God, Lord of the Ascending Stairways, he said: The ascending stairs to heaven. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement the Possessor of the Ascents, he said: God is the Possessor of the Ascents. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Dhi Al-Ma’arij means: Dhi Al-Daraj.
70:4: And His statement, The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years, God Almighty says: The angels and the Spirit, who is Gabriel, peace be upon him, ascend to Him, meaning to God Almighty, and the ha in His statement, to Him refers back to the name of God, on a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years, meaning: The extent of their ascension in that day for other creation was fifty thousand years, and that is because they ascend from the end of a matter from below the seventh earth to the end of His matter from above the seven heavens. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Amr bin Maruf, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: The end of His command is below the earth to the end of His command above the heavens and the earth is the extent of a year, and a Day is the extent of a thousand years. By that he means the descent of the command from the heaven to the earth, and from the earth to the heaven in one day, so that is the extent of a thousand years, because the distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The angels and the spirit ascend to Him on a day when He completes judgment among His creation. The duration of that day on which He completes judgment among them is fifty thousand years. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah: On a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. He said: In one day, the judgment will be completed on that day, like the moon of fifty thousand years. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, On a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. He said: The Day of Resurrection. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding this verse, fifty thousand years, he said: the Day of Resurrection. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. That is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. Muammar said: It was also conveyed to me on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, its duration is fifty thousand years, no one knows how much has passed or how much remains except God. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years, this is the Day of Resurrection, which God has made for the disbelievers the extent of fifty thousand years. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, meaning the Day of Resurrection. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: This is the Day of Resurrection. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Diraj told him, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Sa`id, that he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. How long this is! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is made easy for the believer until it is lighter for him than the obligatory prayer he prays in this world. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in this regard other than the statement we mentioned about him, and that is what: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, that a man asked Ibn Abbas about a day whose length was a thousand years. He said: What is a day whose length was fifty thousand years? He said: I only asked you so that you would tell me. He said: They are two days that God mentioned in the Qur’an. God knows best about them. So he was reluctant to say about the Book of God what he did not know. Ibn Bashar told us: Abdul Wahhab told us: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, who said: A man asked Ibn Abbas about a day whose duration was a thousand years. He was asked about it, What is a day whose duration was fifty thousand years? He said, I only asked you so that you would inform me. He said, “They are two days that God, the Almighty, the Majestic, mentioned. God knows best about them, and I hate to say about the Book of God what I do not know.” The majority of the reciters of the regions read the verse, The angels and the Spirit ascend, with a ta’, except for Al-Kisa’i, who used to read it with a ya’, based on a report he narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he read it in this way. The correct reading for us is what the reciters of the regions do, which is with the letter ta’, because the authoritative reciters agree on it.
70:5: His statement, So be patient with beautiful patience. God Almighty says: So be patient with beautiful patience, meaning: a patience in which there is no impatience. He is saying to him: Be patient with the harm that these polytheists cause you, and do not let the unpleasantness that you encounter from them prevent you from conveying the message that your Lord has commanded you to convey to them. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement, So be patient with beautiful patience, this was when he was commanding forgiveness of them, not rewarding them. Then when he commanded jihad and harshness with them, he commanded severity and killing until they were left alone, and this was abrogated. What Ibn Zayd said, that forgiveness was commanded by this verse and then abrogated, is a statement without basis, because there is no evidence for the correctness of what he said from some of the aspects from which claims are valid. And there is nothing in the command of God to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to be patient in beautiful patience in the harm of the polytheists that necessitates that this was a command from Him to him in some circumstances. Rather, it was a command from God to him in all circumstances, because he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from the time of his mission until He chose him, continued to be harmed by them, and throughout all of that he was patient in the face of the harm he suffered from them, before God gave him permission to fight them, and after His permission to do so.
70:6: God Almighty says: These polytheists see the punishment they asked about, which will befall them, as being far from happening. God Almighty only informed us that they see it as being far away because they did not believe in it and denied the resurrection after death, and the reward and punishment. So He said: They see it as not happening, but We see it as being near, because it will happen, and everything that is coming is near. The ha and the mim in his saying they are from the mention of the disbelievers, and the ha in his saying they see it is from the mention of the torment.
70:7: His saying And we see it soon
70:8: And His statement, On the Day the sky will be like molten brass, God Almighty says: On the Day the sky will be like something molten. I have explained the meaning of molten brass previously with supporting evidence, the disagreements of those who disagreed about it, and mentioned what the early Muslims said about it, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, On the Day the sky will be like molten brass, he said: like turbid oil. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On the Day when the sky will be like molten brass, that on that day it will turn another color, red.
70:9: His saying, And the mountains will be like wool. He says, And the mountains will be like wool. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, like wool, he said: like wool. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, like wool, he said: like wool.
70:10: His statement: “And no close friend will ask a close friend. They will see them.” God Almighty says: And no close friend will ask a close friend about his affair because he is preoccupied with his own affairs. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His statement, And no intimate friend will ask about his intimate friend, means that every person is preoccupied with himself and not with the people.
70:11: And His statement: They see them. The people of interpretation differed regarding those meant by the ha and the mim in His statement They see them. Some of them said: What is meant by that are the relatives, that they know their relatives, and every person knows his relative, so that is God’s seeing them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They will see them, he said: They will recognize each other, and they will recognize each other, then they will flee from each other. He said: For each person, that Day, will be a matter that will make him indifferent to others (Abasa 80:37). Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They see them means they know them, they know. By God, a people will know another people, and people will know another people. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that is that the believers see the infidels. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Al-Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement they see them means the believers see the disbelievers. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that are the infidels who were followers of others in this world in disbelief, that they know him as the one followed in Hell. Mention who said that. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They will see them, he said: They will see those who led them astray in this world in the Fire. The first of the sayings regarding this is the most correct. It was said by those who said: The meaning of this is: And a close friend will not ask a close friend about his affair, but they will see them and recognize them, then some of them will flee from others, as God Almighty said: “The Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children. Every man, that Day, will have enough to make him indifferent to others.” (Abasa 80:34-35-36-37) We said that this is the most correct of the interpretations, because it is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, and that is that His statement, They will see them, followed His statement, And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend. So the ha’ and the mim are more similar to the mention of them than to the mention of others. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement nor is he asked. The majority of reciters in the regions, except for Abu Ja`far al-Qari` and Shaiba, read it with a fat-ha on the ya`. Abu Ja`far and Shaiba read it nor is he asked with a damma on the ya`, meaning: it is not said to a close friend, Where is your close friend? nor are some of them asked of others. The correct reading in our opinion is to open the Ya, meaning: people should not ask each other about his business, because the meaning of that is correct, and because the authoritative reciters of the Qur’an agree on it. God Almighty says: On that Day, the disbelievers will wish and desire that he could ransom himself from God’s punishment on that Day with his children, his wife, his brother, his clan, the tribe that shelters him, and all of creation on earth, so that this may save him from God’s punishment on that Day. And He, the Most High, began by mentioning sons, then companions, then brothers, informing His servants that the unbeliever, due to the great calamity that will befall him on that Day, will redeem himself, if he finds a way to do so, by means of the people he loves most in this world, and the closest to him in lineage. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, The sinner would wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his children, his wife, his brother, and his clan who sheltered him, the most beloved, the most beloved, the closest, the closest of his family and clan, due to the hardships of that Day. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and his clan that sheltered him, he said: his tribe. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, and his companion, he said: The companion is the wife, and his clan who shelters him, he said: His clan is his tribe.
70:12: His saying and his companion and his brother
70:13: His saying and his clan that shelters him
70:14: His saying, And everyone on earth, then He will save him.
70:15: God Almighty says: No, that is not so. Nothing will save him from God’s punishment. Then He began to tell of what He had prepared for him there, may He be glorified, and said, It is a blazing fire. Blazing fire is one of the names of Hell, and that is why it was not in the accusative case. The Arabists differed about its position. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its position is in the accusative case as a substitute for the ha’, and the predicate of inna is niza’ah. He said: If you wish, you can make laza nominative as the predicate of inna, and raise niza’ah as the subject. Some of those who denied that said: It is not appropriate to follow the apparent implied except in anomalies. He said: The test is inna laza * niza’ah ash-shuwa it is a flame * niza’ah ash-shuwa laza is the predicate, and niza’ah is a state. He said: And whoever raises it starts again, because it is praise or blame. He said: And it is not a subject except in this way. The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that laza is the predicate, and nza’ah is the subject, so that is in the nominative case, and the accusative case is not permissible in the recitation due to the consensus of the reciters of the regions on raising it, and no reciter read like that in the accusative case, even though the accusative case in Arabic has a face. It may be possible that the ha’ in the saying inha is an imaad, and laza’ah is in the nominative case with nza’ah, and nza’ah with lazi, just as it is said: inha hind qa’imah, and innahu hind qa’imah, so the ha’ is an imaad in both cases.
70:16: And His statement: Tearing off the skin of the head God Almighty says, informing about the flames as it tears off the scalp and the extremities of the body. And the word shawā is all shawāt, and it is from the limbs of the human being as long as it is not fatal. It is said: He shot and roasted: if he did not hit a fatal target. So perhaps the describer described the scalp being torn off, as Al-A’sha said: The dead woman said: What is wrong with him that his hair has turned white? Perhaps the leg is described in this way, as they say in describing the horse: Abel Al-Shawa, the breast of the butcher He means by that: his lists, and the origin of all of that is what I described. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about Naz’at al-Shuwa. He said: It removes the mother of the head. Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Sawaaf told us: Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan Al-Ashqar told us: Yahya bin Muhallab Abu Kadina told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, pulling out the hair, he said, pulling out the head. Muhammad bin Saada told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, tearing off the flesh means the skins and the heads. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, tearing off the hair he said: the skins of the head. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, who said: I asked Saeed ibn Jubayr about his statement, tearing off the flesh, but he did not provide any information. So I asked Mujahid about it, and I said, The flesh without the bone? He said, Yes. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh, Naz’at al-Shuwa, he said: The leg meat. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said: Qubaysah bin Uqbah Al-Suwa’i told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, that which pulls out the flesh of the legs, he said: that which pulls out the flesh of the legs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Qura bin Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: The one who removes the roasting he said: For the head, it burns some of it, but his heart remains tender. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Qurra told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, a stripper of the flesh, then he mentioned something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, pulling out the hair means pulling out his head, his noble character, and his extremities. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, It strips away the flesh and skin from the bones, leaving nothing of it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, pulling out the flesh, he said: The flesh is the large, fleshy flesh, that is the flesh. And his saying, Naz’ah, he said: Their bones will be cut as you see, then their creation will be renewed and their skins will be changed.
70:17: And his saying, It calls to itself whoever turned away and turned away, means: It calls to itself the flame of hell whoever turned away in this world from obeying God and turned away from believing in His Book and His Messengers. The people of interpretation said the same thing as we said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, You call whoever turns away and turns away, he said: from obeying God, and turns away, he said: from the Book of God, and from His right. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, You call whoever turns away and turns away, he said: from the truth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, It calls whoever turns away and turns away, he said: It has no authority except over the humiliation of whoever disbelieves, turns away and turns away from God. As for whoever believes in God and His Messenger, then it has no authority over him.
70:18: And his saying, And he gathered and stored it, means: He gathered money and put it in a container, and withheld God’s right from it, so he did not pay zakat or spend it on what God had obligated him to spend it on. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, and he gathered and stored he said: he gathered the money. Muhammad bin Mansur al-Tusi told us: Abu Qatan told us: Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said: Abdullah bin Ukaim did not tie his bag. He said: I heard God say: And he gathered and stored. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And he gathered and stored was a group of people who were able to do evil.
70:19: God Almighty says: Indeed, man the disbeliever was created anxious. Panic means worry combined with intense anxiety and impatience. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, man was created impatient, he said: He is the one about whom God said, When evil touches him, impatient, * And when good touches him, withholding [it]. And he says: The impatient is the impatient and greedy, and this is about the polytheists. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ab ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Hubayr: Indeed, man was created impatient. He said: Stingy and impatient. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah: Indeed, man was created anxious. He said: Impatient. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Verily, man meaning the disbeliever was created impatient, meaning: he is stingy, withholding good things, and impatient when a calamity befalls him. This is the impatient one. Yahya bin Habib bin Arabi told us: Khalid bin Al-Harith told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of His Eminence, Yahya said: Khalid said: I asked Shu’bah about His statement, Indeed, man was created impatient, so Shu’bah told me, on the authority of His Eminence, that he said: The impatient is the greedy. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Sa’na, who said: I asked Hasin about this verse: Indeed, man was created anxious. He said: Eager. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, man was created impatient, he said: Impatient means anxious. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, He was created anxious, he said: Impatient.
70:20: And his saying, If evil touches him, he is impatient, means: If his wealth decreases and poverty and destitution befall him, he is impatient of that and cannot bear it.
70:21: And if good befalls him, he withholds it. He says: And if his money increases and he becomes rich, he is withholding what he has, miserly with it, not spending it in obedience to God, nor fulfilling God's right over it.
70:22: And His statement, Except for those who pray, who are constant in their prayers, means: Except for those who obey God by performing what He has enjoined upon them of prayer, and they are constant in performing it, not wasting any of it. For those are not included among those who were created anxious, and yet are disbelieving in their Lord and do not pray to God. It was said: What was meant by the statement except those who pray were the believers who were with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said that it meant everyone who prayed the five prayers. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Ar-Rahman and Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: Those who are constant in their prayers. He said: The obligatory prayers. Zurayq bin Al-Sakhb told me, he said: Muawiyah bin Amr told us, he said: Zaidah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, Those who are constant in their prayers, he said: the five daily prayers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, man was created impatient, until his statement, perpetually. He mentioned to us that Daniel described Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: They perform a prayer such that if the people of Noah had performed it, they would not have drowned, or if the people of Aad had not sent upon them the barren wind, or if the people of Thamud had not been seized by the blast. So adhere to prayer, for it is a good characteristic of the believers. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: They are constant in their prayers. He said: The prescribed prayer. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn al-Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Those who are constant in their prayers, he said: These are the believers who are with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, constant in their prayers. He said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Haywa told us on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Abu al-Khair, that he asked Uqbah bin Amir al-Juhani, about those who are constant in their prayers. He said: They are those who, when they pray, do not turn behind them, nor to their right, nor to their left. Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid told me, saying: My father told me, saying: Al-Awza’i told us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, saying: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Aisha, the wife of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do as much good deeds as you can bear, for God does not get tired until you get tired. She said: “The most beloved deeds to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were those that he performed consistently.” Abu Salamah said: “God says: ‘Those who are constant in their prayers.’”
70:23: His saying: Those who are constant in their prayers.
70:24: God Almighty says: Except for those in whose wealth there is a temporary right, which is zakat for the beggar who asks from his wealth, and the deprived one who has been deprived of wealth, so he is poor and does not ask. The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of the known truth that God mentioned in this topic. Some of them said: It is zakat. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told me, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And those in whose wealth there is a recognized right * For the beggar and the deprived, he said: The recognized right is zakat. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And those in whose wealth there is a recognized right, he said: The obligatory zakat. Others said: Rather, it is a right other than zakat. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And those in whose wealth there is a recognized right * For the beggar and the deprived, he said: It is other than charity with which one maintains kinship ties, or with which one entertains a guest, or with which one carries a load, or with which one helps the deprived. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Yunus, on the authority of Rabah bin Ubaydah, on the authority of Qaz’ah, that Ibn Umar was asked about the statement, In their wealth is a known right * For the needy and the deprived. Is it zakat? He said, You have other rights besides that. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Ibn Fadil told us: Bayan told us on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: There is a right to money other than zakat. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: There is a right in wealth other than zakat. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid: In their wealth there is a known right. He said: other than zakat. They agreed that the questioner is the one whose characteristics were described. They also differed about the meaning of deprived in this topic, similar to their difference about it in Adh-Dhariyat. We mentioned what they said about it there, and we provided evidence for what is correct in our view. However, we will mention some of the reports that we did not mention there. Mention of those who said: It is the letters. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Al-Aizar, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: The deprived one is the one who is corrupted. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muslim bin Khalid told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The deprived one is the one who is corrupted. Sahl bin Musa Al-Razi told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The beggar and the deprived means the one who has no share in Islam. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The deprived one is the one who has no share in Islam. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us: Yazid ibn Zari` told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Qays ibn Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: For the beggar and the deprived. He said: The beggar is the one who asks, and the deprived is the one who is deprived. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, he said: I heard Abu Ishaq narrating on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said regarding this verse, For the beggar and the deprived. He said: The beggar is the one who asks, and the deprived is the one who is deprived. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais ibn Karkam, he said: I asked Ibn Abbas, about his statement, for the beggar and the deprived. He said: The beggar is the one who asks, and the deprived is the one who is deviated from the path and has no share in Islam. Muhammad bin Omar bin Ali Al-Muqaddami told me: Quraysh bin Anas told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: The deprived: the one who is corrupted. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Quraysh told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, the same. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about the deprived, and he did not say anything about it. He said: And Ata’ said: It is the forbidden limits. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Qais bin Karkam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the one who has no share in Islam, and he is a deviant among the people. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The deprived one is the one who is not given anything and is deprived. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The deprived one is the one who seeks the world and it turns away from it, so he does not ask people. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said about the deprived: He is the one who is deprived and has no one to take care of him or give him anything. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The deprived one is the one who has no booty in Islam, and he is at war with the people. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ali told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’: The deprived one is the one who is corrupted. Others said: He is the one who has no share in the spoils. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, that some people came to Ali, may God be pleased with him, in Kufa after the Battle of the Camel, and he said: Divide it for them, and he said: This is the deprived one. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The deprived one is the one who is deprived and has no right to anything from the spoils. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. He said: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim al-Jadali, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin al-Hanafiyyah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a raiding party, and they took spoils, and he conquered them. Then some people came who had not witnessed it, so the verse was revealed: In their wealth is a recognized right, for the needy and the deprived, meaning these people. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a military expedition and they captured spoils. Then some people came who had not witnessed the spoils, so the verse was revealed: In their wealth is a recognized right * For the needy and the deprived. Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim Al-Jadali, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad, who said: A raiding party was sent out and they captured spoils, then a group of people came after them. He said: Then the verse for the beggar and the deprived was revealed. Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Naim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad, that some people during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, acquired spoils of war. Then some people came after that, and the following verse was revealed: In their wealth is a known right, for the needy and the deprived. Others said: He is the one whose money does not grow. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, he said: I asked Ikrimah about the beggar and the deprived. He said: The beggar is the one who asks you, and the deprived is the one who does not have money to grow. Others said: He is the one whose money has been stolen. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, on the authority of Wahb bin Jarir, who said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: Sail bin Al-Yamamah came and took some money to a man. A man from among the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the deprived one. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and the deprived, he said: The deprived is the one whose fruit and crops are afflicted. And he recited, Have you seen what you till? Is it you who sow it? (al-Waqi’ah 56:64)... until he reached deprived (al-Waqi’ah 56:67). And the companions of Paradise said, “Indeed, we are astray. Rather, we are deprived.” (al-Qalam 68:27). Al-Shaabi said: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said: Al-Sha’bi said: I was unable to know what the deprived is. Qatada said: Ibn Bashar told me: Abd al-A’la told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, for the beggar and the deprived, he said: The beggar is the one who asks with his hand, and the deprived is the one who is too chaste, and both of them have a right over you, O son of Adam. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, K told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, for the beggar and the deprived, which is a beggar who asks you for something in his hand, and a poor person who is self-sufficient and does not ask people, and both of them have a right over you.
70:25: His saying: For the beggar and the deprived.
70:26: And the statement, And those who believe in the Day of Judgment, means: Except for those who acknowledge the resurrection and recompense.
70:27: And His statement, And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord, and those who are in this world afraid of the punishment of their Lord and fear that He will punish them in the Hereafter, so out of fear of that they do not see any obligation for it, nor do they transgress its limits.
70:28: And His saying, Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not secure, means that it will not befall those who disobey Him and go against His command.
70:29: God the Most High says: And those who guard their private parts meaning they guard their private parts from everything that God has forbidden them to put in it, except that they are not to be blamed for not guarding them from their wives or those their right hands possess of female slaves. It was also said: They guard their private parts * except from their wives and this was not preceded by a denial because the statement they are not to be blamed indicates that there is a meaning of denial in the speech, and that is like the saying of the one who says: Do whatever you want except committing a sin, for you will be punished for it, and its meaning is: Do whatever you want except that you will be punished for committing a sin.
70:30: His saying, Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed.
70:31: And His statement, But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors. So whoever seeks a wife other than his wife, or the possession of his right hand, then those who do that are the transgressors, who have transgressed what was permissible for them to what was forbidden to them, so they are the ones to be blamed.
70:32: God Almighty says: Except for those who are watchful of the trusts of God which He has entrusted to them of His obligations and the trusts of His servants which they have been entrusted with, and His covenants which He took from them to obey Him in what He has commanded them and forbidden them, and the covenants of His servants which He has given them regarding what He has made a covenant with them upon Himself, they watch over that and preserve it and do not waste it, but they fulfill it and pledge to it in accordance with what God has obligated them and made obligatory upon them to preserve it.
70:33: And those who uphold their testimonies means those who do not conceal what they testify to, but rather they perform it, as it is required of them to perform it, without changing or altering it.
70:34: And those who maintain their prayers He says: And those who maintain the times of their prayers that God has imposed upon them and the limits that He has made obligatory upon them, and do not waste any of their times or limits.
70:35: And His saying, Those will be in gardens, honored. God Almighty says: Those who do these deeds will be in honored gardens, and God will honor them with His honor.
70:36: God Almighty says: What is the matter with those who disbelieved in God before you, O Muhammad, that they are rushing about? We have already explained the meaning of rushing about and what the scholars of interpretation have said about it in the past, so there is no need to repeat it here. However, we will mention in this place some of what we did not mention there. Qatada said about it: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then why are those who disbelieved before you rushing about? He means deliberately. Ibn Zayd said about it: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then why are those who disbelieved before you hastening on? He said: Mahta’a means the one who does not blink. Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the Arabic language used to say: Mahnaha means hasty. And he narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan what: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amer told us: Qara told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Then why are those who disbelieved before you rushing forward? He said: Going forth. Ibn Bashar told us: Hammad bin Mas’adah told us: Qara told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same.
70:37: And his saying, On the right and on the left, in groups, means: On your right, O Muhammad, and on your left, dispersed in circles and gatherings, group by group, turning away from you and from the Book of God. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of Yawil said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saeed told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Then what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you that they are rushing about He said: Before you, they were looking on the right and on the left in groups He said: The groups are the people on the right and on the left, turning away from him, mocking him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, on the right and on the left in groups, he said: gatherings of people who are away from each other. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you that they rushed headlong means: deliberately to the right and to the left in groups meaning in groups around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, not interested in the Book of God nor in His Prophet. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, ‘Azzin, he said: ‘Azzin are the circles and gatherings. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ibn Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, two groups, that he said: circles and companions. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, On the right and on the left, in groups, he said: The group of three and four is the group, and the group of three and four is those of the group of two. Ismail bin Musa Al-Fazari told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Why do I see you in two groups? And Al-Azin means the scattered rings. Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Shaqiq told us, on the authority of Abdullah al-Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to his companions who were in circles, and said: Why do I see you so divided? Abu Husayn told me, he said: Ubaydhar told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Tamim bin Tarfa Al-Ta’i, on the authority of Jabir bin Samurah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us while we were dispersing, and he said: What is wrong with you that you are separated? Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Amr Al-Ghazi told me, he said: Al-Faryabi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Tamim bin Tarfa, on the authority of Jabir bin Samra, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to some of his companions while they were sitting, and he said: What is the matter with you that I see you in two groups? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Tamim bin Tarfa, on the authority of Jabir bin Samurah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to some of his companions while they were sitting, and he said: Why do I see you in two groups? Ibn Hamid told me: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Tamim bin Tarfa Al-Ta’i, who said: Jabir bin Samurah told us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them while they were in groups, and said: Why do I see you in groups? He said: In groups, meaning his statement: on the right and on the left in groups. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Qurra told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, On the right and on the left in two groups, he said: Two groups: dispersed, going right and left, saying: What did this man say! Ibn Bashar told us: Hamid bin Masada told us: Qara told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, similarly. The singular of ‘azin is ‘azza, just as the singular of thabain is thaba, and the singular of karin is karah. And from ‘azin is the saying of the camel’s shepherd: Khalifa Al-Rahman, my tribe has become proud and strong
70:38: And His statement, Does every man among them aspire to enter a garden of delights? He says: Does every man among those who disbelieved before you aspire to be admitted by God into a garden of delights? That is, gardens of delights in which he can enjoy himself. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, that he may enter a Garden of Delight. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as enters with a damma on the ya’ in the manner of what the agent was not named, except for al-Hasan and Talha ibn Musarraf, as it was mentioned from them that they used to recite it with a fatha on the ya’, meaning: every man among them, that every man among them may enter a Garden of Delight. The correct reading in this regard is what the readers of Al-Attar do, which is to add the ya’ due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on this.
70:39: And His saying, No indeed! We created them from what they know. The Almighty says: The matter is not as these infidels hope for, that every person among them will enter a paradise of bliss. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, We created them from that which they know, you were only created from filth, O son of Adam, so fear God.
70:40: God Almighty says: I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests of the earth, ‘Indeed, We are able* to replace them with better ones.’ He says: We are able to destroy them and bring forth better ones from among the creation who will obey Me and not disobey Me. And We will not be outdone. God Almighty says: And not one of them can escape Us with a command that We desire from him, so that he escapes Us. And we said something similar to that, and the people of interpretation said that. Who said that? Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Anarah ibn Abi Hafsah told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Ibn Abbas said: The sun rises every year in three hundred and sixty windows, and does not return to that window until that day of the following year, and it does not rise except reluctantly, saying: O Lord, do not let me see Your servants, for I see them disobeying You, committing sins against You, I see them. He said: Have you not heard the words of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: Until you drag and flog I said: O my master, and he flogs the sun? He said: I bit your father with them. The narrator only forced him to flog. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Amara told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Lord of the Easts and the Wests, he said: The sun rises from three hundred and sixty places, rising every day from a place of rising and does not return to it the next day, and it does not rise except reluctantly. Ikrimah said: So I said to him: The poet said: Until you drag and flog He said: Ibn Abbas said: I bit your father with them, but the narrator forced him to do so. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr told us: Shu’bah told us: Ammarah told us, on the authority of Ikrim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The sun rises in three hundred and sixty windows, and if it rises in a window, it does not rise from it until the following year, and it does not rise except reluctantly. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests, he said: He is the rising of the sun and its setting, and the rising of the moon and its setting place.
70:41: His saying: On the condition that We replace them with better ones, and We will not be outdone.
70:42: And His statement, So leave them to plunge into vain talk and play, is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So leave these polytheists who are rushing about, right and left, vainly delving into their falsehood and playing in this world, until they meet their Day which they are promised, meaning: until they meet the punishment of the Day of Resurrection which they are promised.
70:43: And His statement, The Day they come forth, is an explanation and guidance of the first day which is in His statement, The Day they are promised. The interpretation of the statement is: until they meet the Day they are promised, the Day they come forth from the graves, which are the tombs: the singular of which is jadath, “in haste as if they were hastening toward a place of assembly.” As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, On the Day they will emerge from the graves quickly, meaning from the graves quickly. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. We have already explained the grave before with its supporting evidence and what the scholars have said about it. And his statement, to a monument they hasten, meaning: as if they were racing towards a flag that had been erected for them. The reciters of the regions agreed unanimously to open the noon in his statement an-nazb except for al-Hasan al-Basri, as it was mentioned from him that he used to close it with the sad, and it is as if the one who opened it directed the nasb to it being a source from the saying of the speaker: I set the thing up, I set it up, and it is as if its interpretation for them is as if they are hastening to an erected idol, and as for the one who closed it with the sad, then it is one of the idols, and they are their gods that they used to worship. As for his saying they hasten, “ifād” means to hasten, and from it the poet said: I swear by the ostrich that always goes out and seeks to be treated with kindness. He says: You seek refuge to which you can resort, and ifād means speed. Ru’bah said: Grandfather walks with us on his hands And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Ibn Abi `Uday told us, on the authority of `Awf, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, that he said about this verse, As if they were hastening to a target, he said: They race to landmarks. Muhammad bin Saeed told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, As if they were hastening to a target, he said: They are striving to knowledge. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They hasten, he said: They race. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, As if they were hastening to a place of worship. He said: They were striving to knowledge. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: As if they were hastening towards a target. He said: They were running. Ali bin Sahl told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I heard Abu Omar say: I heard Yahya bin Abi Katheer say: As if they were rushing towards a target. He said: They are racing towards a goal. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, to a place they hasten, to a place they set out. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: To a place they hasten. He said: To knowledge they race. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, As if they were hastening to idols, he said: The idols are stones that they used to worship, tall stones called idols. And regarding His statement, hastening, he said: They hasten to idols that they used to hasten to. Ibn Zayd said: And the idols that the people of ignorance used to worship and visit and venerate, one of them would carry them with him, and if he saw one better than it, he would take it and throw this one down, and He said to it, “Each one follows his master. Wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice while he is on a straight path?” An-Nahl
70:44: And His statement, Their eyes will be humbled, meaning: Their eyes will be submissive to the shame and humiliation they are in. Disgrace will overwhelm them, meaning: Disgrace will overwhelm them. That is the Day which they were promised, meaning: God Almighty says: This is the Day whose description I have described, and it is the Day of Resurrection which the polytheists of Quraysh were promised in this world, that they would have no power in the Hereafter. They used to lie about it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: That day is the Day of Resurrection which they were promised.
